meta.purpose: Ledger of specific news claims the nightly scanner has already verified as misdated (the underlying event is real, but its true date is a year or more away from the date implied by the aggregator/republication that surfaced it). Created for backlog item SC-1 / defect class DC-13, opened after the Meta '8,000 layoffs' claim and the China 'Ethnic Unity Law' claim each recurred and were re-verified from scratch across multiple nightly cycles, and after 8 of the 14 candidates dropped on the 2026-09-18 cycle turned out to be the same shape of error.
meta.brief_addendum: Before verifying a candidate's date from scratch, check research/known-misdated-claims.json for an active entry matching this entity. If one matches, you do not need to re-run verification searches -- cite the entry's true_date and source, drop the candidate as already-known, and append today's date to that entry's occurrences[] array (append-only; do not edit or remove prior entries). An entry means 'this specific claim is misdated', not 'this entity is banned' -- the same entity can and will produce genuine, correctly-dated news on a different topic, and that must still be flagged normally. validate-scan.mjs enforces this: it fails the scan if a top_entities candidate matches an active ledger entry's matcher, but a correctly-dropped candidate never triggers a failure.
meta.how_entries_are_read: See research/scripts/validate-scan.mjs, section 8 (checkKnownMisdatedClaims). Only entries with status 'active' are checked. A candidate is flagged when EVERY token-group in matcher[] has at least one substring hit (case-insensitive) against the concatenated slug+name+news_summary text of a research/scans/<date>.json top_entities item (see section 8c in validate-scan.mjs for exactly which fields of a candidate are read and why -- narrowed 2026-09-21, SC-1c, after a live run showed a candidate's own news_summary can quote ledger vocabulary while correctly explaining it is NOT a match).

claims.description: 'Meta cuts/lays off 8,000 jobs' is a real event, but it happened 2026-05-20, not in September. An undated aggregator snippet keeps getting re-surfaced as if it were new.
claims.claimed_framing: Implies the 8,000-job cut is a fresh September 2026 announcement/execution.
claims.matcher_scope: Requires the Meta entity token AND the specific 8,000 headcount figure AND a job/layoff word, all three, regardless of phrasing order (e.g. 'cut 8,000 jobs' and '8,000 job cuts' both match). A genuine, differently-sized Meta layoff (e.g. 12,000 jobs) or a genuine Meta story with no layoff/job content will not match, because at least one required group is absent. The count group (8,000/8000) is the group doing the real specificity work here -- 'job'/'jobs' alone is broad, but combined with Meta AND the exact 8,000 figure it is not a realistic false-positive shape.

claims.description: An FDA Class I correction for BD Alaris Pump Modules (pumps dropped/jarred in shipping, causing 2 serious injuries) read as September 2026 news. The 2026-09-24 scan record verifies the customer letter BD sent is dated 2025-10-17 and the reporting MedTech Dive article is dated 2025-12-02 (the FDA record's '09/17/2026' timestamp is a page-metadata update, not new content) -- a year-stale claim relative to a September 2026 scan window.
claims.claimed_framing: Implies the BD Alaris pump Class I correction (dropped/jarred pumps, 2 serious injuries) is a fresh September 2026 FDA action, rather than a correction whose customer letter dates to 2025-10-17 (reported by MedTech Dive on 2025-12-02).
claims.matcher_scope: Requires the Becton Dickinson/BD Alaris entity token AND a dropped/jarred defect-description token AND a recall/correction token, all three. A genuine, unrelated Becton Dickinson story (earnings, a different product line's recall with no drop/jarring mechanism, an unrelated Alaris feature update) will not match, because at least one required group is absent. Evasion routes documented rather than fixed (SC-1d is backlog, not implemented here): (1) a rewording that describes the defect only as 'impact damage' or 'shipping damage' -- dropping both 'dropped' and 'jarred' -- would evade the second group; (2) a rewording that calls the action a 'field safety notice' or 'urgent medical device letter' without 'recall'/'correction'/'Class I correction' would evade the third group; (3) a rewording that names only the ticker 'BDX' or 'the company' without 'Becton Dickinson' or 'BD Alaris' would evade the first group.

claims.description: A claim that 'President Sisi pardoned activist Alaa Abdel Fattah on September 22' read as 2026-09-22. The 2026-09-24 scan record verifies via HRW, Al Jazeera and Middle East Eye that the pardon occurred 2025-09-22 -- exactly one year before this scan date -- a year-stale claim relative to a September 2026 scan window.
claims.claimed_framing: An undated or year-dropped 'September 22' pardon mention is read as a September 2026 pardon rather than the actual 2025-09-22 pardon.
claims.matcher_scope: Requires the Egypt entity token AND the activist's specific three-word name 'Alaa Abdel Fattah' (or a spelling variant) -- deliberately NOT the bare surname 'Abdel Fattah', which is also part of President Sisi's own name (Abdel Fattah el-Sisi) and would produce a realistic false-positive shape on ordinary Sisi coverage -- AND a pardon token. A genuine, unrelated Egypt story (a Sisi policy announcement, a different Egypt human-rights story with no pardon) will not match. Evasion routes documented rather than fixed: (1) a rewording that refers to him only as 'the British-Egyptian blogger' or 'Alaa' without the 'Abdel Fattah' surname would evade the second group; (2) a rewording that says he was 'released' or 'freed' rather than 'pardoned' would evade the third group. Proven not to collide with egypt-ismail-al-iskandrani-arrest below: this entry's matcher requires 'alaa abdel fattah' + pardon language, neither of which appears in a genuine al-Iskandrani arrest item, and that entry's matcher requires 'iskandrani' + arrest/detention language, neither of which appears in a genuine Alaa Abdel Fattah pardon item -- see test-known-misdated-claims.mjs's two-Egypt-entries collision test.

claims.claimed_framing: An undated 'issued in September' aggregator summary of the UN Commission of Inquiry's genocide finding is read as a September 2026 report rather than the actual 2025-09-16 publication.
claims.matcher_scope: Requires an Israel/Gaza entity token AND the distinctive 'Commission of Inquiry' UN-body phrase AND the word 'genocide', all three. A genuine, unrelated Israel/Gaza story (a ceasefire development, a diplomatic story, or even a genuine current story that uses the word 'genocide' without the Commission-of-Inquiry framing -- plausible given Israel's own index entry already documents an ICJ 'plausible genocide' finding as ongoing context) will not match, because the distinctive 'Commission of Inquiry' phrase is absent. Evasion routes documented rather than fixed: (1) a rewording that calls the body 'the UN inquiry panel' or 'UN investigators' without the exact 'Commission of Inquiry' phrase would evade the second group; (2) a rewording that uses 'crimes against humanity' or 'war crimes' instead of 'genocide' would evade the third group; (3) conversely, because the same Commission of Inquiry issues periodic reports on other dates, a genuinely NEW Commission of Inquiry report that also uses the word 'genocide' would still match this entry and require a human to check whether it restates the 2025-09-16 report or is a distinct later one -- flagged as a known over-match risk, not resolved here.

claims.notes: The scan record's own suggested matcher candidate was 'israel'/'gaza' + 'commission of inquiry'/'genocide' + '69,000' or '65,000' (a casualty-figure group). This entry does not require the casualty-figure group because the reported death toll is a running count that could plausibly reach a similar figure in genuinely new September 2026 reporting, which would make a casualty-figure requirement either a false-negative risk (if the true figure is later revised) or, if loosened into a range, exactly the warn-level matching this brief prohibits implementing here. Proposed, not implemented: a second, deliberately looser pattern keyed on 'commission of inquiry' + 'genocide' + the exact substring 'more than 69,000' (rather than the bare number, which is more collision-prone) could tighten precision further if this claim resurfaces reworded; left as a follow-up per the brief's instruction not to implement warn-level matching in this pass.
